purpose: Say whether the WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS environment variable still fails to open the window's debugging port on the same elevated Windows runner where the policy-value route passes

source.step: Control, informational (Windows) - one flow with the port requested by the environment variable only
source.note: this file is a summary of that artifact; the artifact itself holds runner temp paths and is kept as an Actions artifact, not committed

method: Same job, right after the package flows. One flow (refuse_bad_inputs) from the release build, with MDD_WEBVIEW2_POLICY unset, so the driver asks for the port only through the environment variable. The driver first printed that its own policy value was already removed.

control_outcome.error_first_line: Error: no page target on port 9401 within 30 s (the port was requested through the WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS environment variable)
control_outcome.loopback_probe: 127.0.0.1, [::1] and localhost all refused the connection

reading: On this elevated runner with WebView2 Runtime 156.0.4314.58 the environment variable does not reach the browser process, and a machine policy value named after the host exe does. This matches Microsoft's documented behaviour for an elevated host (concepts/security, 'For an elevated host app, use appropriate override flags'). It was observed for the environment variable on 156 only: an earlier run on Runtime 157.0.4341.46 passed with the policy route and has no environment-variable control.
